summary:
Two flat-topped west towers (x 2..22, top y 95, parapet to 97), then nave and choir (clerestory eave y 47) under one continuous lead ridge at y 59, transept roses north and south, an octagonal deepslate spire at the crossing with copper apostles and its rooster tip at exactly y 137.
It reads as Notre-Dame from the river: a semicircular east end (apse) ringed by five gabled chapels, buttress piers standing 3 blocks proud with pinnacles, and long one-block flying buttresses with open sky under them.
Pale cream sandstone against dark lead roofs, deep window reveals with lit stained glass, and floodlights at the pier feet for dusk; every mass stays within the footprint and height limits. Notre-Dame from the river: pale smooth/cut sandstone cathedral with flat-topped west towers (y 95-97), one continuous lead nave+choir roof (ridge 59) and transept roses, a hand-built half-decagon apse with five gabled radiating chapels. The relief is the hero: 3-proud set-off piers with pinnacles, 30 one-block flying buttresses with sky under them, gargoyles, corbel tables and parapets on the south flank and chevet.
An octagonal deepslate spire with copper apostles ends in the rooster at (94,137,38); stained glass glows from shroomlights behind it, ochre froglight floodlights sit at the pier feet and lanterns stand on the set-offs for dusk.

parts.name: P1 Masonry shell
parts.scope: All masses M1..M21 except the spire: plinths to the GROUND map (plinthCourse), walls (ashlarWall), flankBay tiled over the nave (piers 32..80 + first bay x 23..31) and the choir (104..144) on both sides (N = mirror z'=76-z), transept walls and stone gables (stoneGable peak 57; west gable M4 peak 63), apse (polygonWall), ambulatory rings r 11..19 / 19..26 (polarWall), the five chapels' walls (radialChapel), sacristy blocks, the octagonal stair turret, towers hollow to y 95 with floors at 30/57/62/95, porch base M5. Every pier with set-offs (setoffPier, transept M10, 4 west buttresses, radialPier x6, sacristy buttresses). Every OPENING as air with jambs and heads (lancet, belfryLancet, portal void, roseWindow glass:false); RESERVED cells untouched.

parts.name: P2 Lead roofs
parts.scope: R1 nave+choir (x 23..152, eave 48, ridge 59 at z 38), R2 transept (ridge 57 at x 94), R8 sacristy via $MCD roof gable with the lead mix (keep: spire box x 90..98 z 34..42 y 48..137, flyer zones, pinnacles, apostle stations). By hand: apseRoof (R3 + cross at 152,60..62,38), leanTo / leanToPolar tribune (32->37) and aisle (21->25) roofs, chapel gables (radialChapel roof), leadDeck on both towers at y 95, turret cone 51..54, ridgeCrest iron_bars on R1 y 60 and R2 y 58.

parts.name: P3 West front and towers
parts.scope: Three portals (Virgin z 17..25, Last Judgement z 34..42 with a trumeau at z 38, St Anne z 51..59; doors at x 6) via portal; 28 kingNiche statues at x 2, even z 12..64, y 23..27; stringCourse y 21..22 and 29; west roseWindow centred (x 2, y 39, z 38), r 6; tower blind lancets y 32..45; colonnade Grand Gallery x 2..3, z 10..66, y 48..56; chimera balustrade y 57..58 + gargoyles at the tower corners; belfryLancet louvres + black panes on all faces; tower parapets (balustrade y 96..97) and corner pinnacles to y 97 only; hanging lanterns under the y 57 cornice.

parts.name: P4 Flanks, transept faces and chevet relief
parts.scope: The hero relief: a flyer at every nave and choir pier on both sides (x p, z 64->51 S / 12->25 N, coping y 36->45 per the VOCABULARY table, air beneath), flyerRadial x6 (r 27 y 36 -> r 11 y 45), wallButtress + gargoyle (y 47) at each, a pinnacle on every pier y 39..47 and on the transept buttresses 55..60, stringCourse y 19 + balustrade y 20 on the aisles and ambulatory, corbelTable/cornice/parapet y 46..48 along the clerestory and round the apse, clerestory mullions. Transept faces: portals at z 66 / z 10 with a wimperg to y 26, triforium lancets, south and north roseWindow about (94, 40) r 6 with glass, a small gable rose 3x3 at y 51..53. Chevet chapel wimpergs y 18..25 with corner pinnacles.

parts.name: P5 Spire and apostles
parts.scope: Drum octagonRing x 90..98, z 34..42, y 50..70 (polished_deepslate, deepslate_tiles bands, eight 1x3 glazed lancets y 58..66, deepslate_tile_wall ribs, gablets 67..70); needle 7 wide y 71..85, 5 wide y 86..105, 3 wide y 106..124, 1 wide y 125..133, centred (94, 38), crocket every 3 courses; spireTip: cross arms at y 131, end_rod mast at 134..136, lightning_rod at exactly (94,137,38). 12 apostles: A x 100, z 43..45, feet y 55/54/53; B x 88, same z and y; C z 48, x 99..101, feet y 53/52/51; D z 28, x 89/88/87, feet y 53/52/51.

parts.name: P6 Glass, light and ground
parts.scope: glazeLancet in every window plane (chapels z 65/11, tribunes z 58/18, clerestory z 48/28, triforium, apse, chapels, sacristy, ambulatory), glowBehind (shroomlight) behind every window and rose, floodlight (ochre_froglight flush) 1 out from every south and chevet pier foot and every 6 cells along the west and north, pierLantern on the y 20 set-offs (standing at y 21), on every 4th parapet post at y 49 and y 21, and on the tower decks at y 96; paveStrip in smooth_stone round the walls. Then $MCD light + $MCD check until no walkable surface is dark.

recruit.why: Coursed ashlar on a 2-thick shell, plinths down to the rock, set-off buttress piers and pointed openings left as air on an 8-block bay rhythm
Steep lead roofs: the roof tool for the gables, hand-built lean-tos, the polar apse cone and chapel gables, kept clear of the flyer zones and the spire box
Portals with stepped archivolts and tympana, the Gallery of Kings, colonnades, chimeras and the west rose tracery
Open one-block flying buttresses with sky under them, pinnacles, gargoyles, corbel tables, wimpergs and the transept roses: the relief the river view reads
parts: P4 Flanks, transept faces and chevet relief

recruit.why: An octagonal needle that tapers in stages, crockets, the copper apostles and a rooster tip exactly at y 137
Stained glass in every lancet and rose with pane connections, plus the belfry louvres
Dusk lighting: froglight floodlights at the pier feet, shroomlight glow behind the glass, and lanterns on the set-offs and parapets so no walkable surface spawns mobs
